types.rule_es: Describen cómo se hace una acción. Normalmente van después del verbo o después del objeto: 'She speaks English fluently'. Nunca entre el verbo y su objeto (no: 'She speaks fluently English').
types.formation_es: Adjetivo + -ly (slow → slowly). Cambios: -y → -ily (easy → easily), -le → -ly (gentle → gently), -ic → -ically (automatic → automatically; excepción: public → publicly), -ue → -uly (true → truly). Irregulares: good → well; fast, hard, high, straight y early no cambian. Adjetivos en -ly (friendly, lovely, silly) no tienen adverbio: se dice 'in a friendly way'.

items.ex: She finished the reading test quickly and left early.
Please speak slowly; I'm still learning English.
Read the instructions carefully before you start the exam.
He drove carelessly and hit the car in front of him.
You can easily get to the old town by bus.
The children played happily in the park all afternoon.
The students worked quietly during the exam.
My neighbor plays music loudly every Saturday night.
She sings really well; she should join a band.
Our team played badly and lost three to zero.
My mother works hard to support our family.
He drives too fast on the highway.
The bride's dress was beautifully made by hand.
The customer shouted angrily at the waiter.
She politely asked the man to turn down his music.
We waited patiently for the doctor for two hours.
Hold the baby gently and support her head.
After two years in Canada, Juan speaks English fluently.
Did I pronounce your name correctly?
You need to take your studies more seriously.
We were watching TV when the lights suddenly went out.
The plane landed safely in spite of the storm.
He laughed nervously before his job interview.
They secretly planned a surprise party for their teacher.
Our hosts welcomed us warmly when we arrived.
Sit up straight and look at the camera, please.
The doors open automatically when you get close.
The mayor publicly apologized for the delays.
I am truly grateful for your help this year.
The price of avocados rose dramatically last month.
The waiter cheerfully brought us more coffee.
Spend your money wisely when you travel.
I accidentally deleted all the photos from my phone.
The old man kindly showed us the way to the station.
The eagle flew high above the mountains.
We left early to avoid the traffic on the highway.
I think he deliberately ignored my message.
The bus arrived late, so I missed my first class.

types.rule_es: Dicen con qué frecuencia pasa algo. Las palabras sueltas (always, usually, never...) van antes del verbo principal pero después de 'be': 'I always walk' / 'She is always late'. Las expresiones (once a week, every day...) van al final o al inicio de la oración.
types.formation_es: La mayoría son palabras fijas (always, often, never). Algunas vienen de adjetivos + -ly (usual → usually, frequent → frequently, rare → rarely). daily, weekly, monthly y yearly tienen la misma forma como adjetivo y adverbio. Las expresiones se forman con número + times + a + periodo (twice a month) o every + periodo (every day). Las marcadas como expresión llevan expr: true.

items.ex: I always drink a cup of coffee before work.
We usually have lunch at one o'clock.
I normally walk to the office, but today I took a taxi.
Students generally prefer classes in the morning.
Do you often go to the cinema on weekends?
This bus is frequently late during the rainy season.
Sometimes I cook dinner for the whole family.
We occasionally eat out on Saturday nights.
My grandfather rarely watches television these days.
She seldom complains about her difficult job.
I hardly ever drink soda anymore.
I have never been to Europe, but I want to go.
Have you ever tried ajiaco from Bogotá?
My phone is constantly ringing during meetings.
You should check your email regularly at work.
The newspaper is published daily, even on holidays.
Our team meets weekly to review the project.
I pay my phone bill monthly by bank transfer.
The flower festival takes place annually in Medellín.
I go to the gym once a week, on Mondays.
We visit our grandparents twice a month.
I study English for twenty minutes every day.
My cousins come to visit us three times a year.
From time to time, I call my old school friends.
We still go dancing now and then.
My little brother asks questions all the time.

items.es: día de por medio / cada dos días
items.ex: She waters the plants every other day.
Once in a while, we order pizza on a Friday night.
I usually sleep late on weekends.

types.rule_es: Dicen cuándo pasa algo. Casi siempre van al final de la oración ('I'll call you tomorrow') o al inicio para dar énfasis. Excepciones: 'already', 'just' y 'still' van antes del verbo principal; 'yet' va al final en preguntas y negativas.
types.formation_es: La mayoría son palabras fijas (now, soon, yet). Algunas vienen de adjetivos + -ly (recent → recently, immediate → immediately). ¡Cuidado! 'late' (tarde) y 'lately' (últimamente) son palabras distintas. Expresiones con last/next/this + periodo no llevan preposición: 'next week', no 'in next week'.

items.ex: I'm busy now; can I call you back in an hour?
I have three classes today and an exam tomorrow.
We are flying to San Andrés tomorrow morning.
I saw your brother at the supermarket yesterday.
Are you coming to the party tonight?
Don't worry, the bus will arrive soon.
I have recently started a new job in Bogotá.
I haven't been sleeping well lately.
I have already finished my homework, Mom.
Has the package from Amazon arrived yet?
Are you still working at the bank downtown?
I have just eaten, so I'm not hungry.
After many tries, they eventually found a solution.
We finally got our visas after three months.
See you later at the party.
I was living in Cali then, so I didn't see the show.
Have you been to this restaurant before?
We had dinner and went dancing afterwards.
Please call me immediately if anything changes.
Nowadays, most people pay with their phones.
She is currently living and working in Canada.
I moved to Bogotá three years ago.
I met him in 2019 and haven't seen him since.
I once met a famous footballer at the airport.
The building was formerly a hospital for children.
I previously worked as a waiter in Medellín.
She doesn't live in this neighborhood anymore.
I can't talk right now; I'm driving.
We're going on vacation to the coast next week.
I watched a great series on TV last night.
The results will be ready the day after tomorrow.
We got up early to catch the six o'clock flight.
The train arrived late again this morning.

types.rule_es: Dicen dónde pasa algo o hacia dónde va. Normalmente van después del verbo o del objeto, al final de la oración: 'The kids are playing outside'. Con verbos de movimiento no llevan 'to': 'go home', 'go abroad', 'go upstairs' (no 'go to home').
types.formation_es: Casi todos son palabras fijas (here, there, abroad) o compuestos (up + stairs, every + where, near + by). No se forman con -ly. ¡Cuidado! 'near' (cerca) no es 'nearly' (casi).

items.ex: Come here and look at this old photo.
I left my keys over there on the kitchen table.
I looked everywhere for my glasses.
There was nowhere to park near the stadium.
Let's go somewhere quiet to talk.

items.es: en ningún lugar (negativas) / en cualquier lugar
items.ex: I can't find my wallet anywhere.

items.es: en otro lugar / en otra parte
items.ex: If this shop is too expensive, we can look elsewhere.
She wants to study abroad next year.

items.es: en el extranjero / al otro lado del mar
items.ex: Many Colombians work overseas and send money home.
The bathroom is upstairs, on the left.
Breakfast is served downstairs from seven to ten.
Is there a good bakery nearby?
Do you live near here, or do you take the bus?
My office isn't far, so I usually walk.
The children are playing outside in the garden.
It's raining, so let's stay inside today.
We had the party indoors because of the rain.
In the dry season we often eat outdoors.
The nearest beach is only twenty minutes away.
I'll be back in five minutes, don't leave.
I usually walk home after work.
Go straight ahead and turn right at the bank.
I left my umbrella behind at the restaurant.
The people in the apartment above make a lot of noise.
Write your answer in the space below.
We walked around for hours in the old city.
In London, you can travel underground on the Tube.
Let's take a taxi downtown tonight.
Please step forward when I call your name.
Come in and sit down, please; dinner is ready.

types.rule_es: Dicen la intensidad de un adjetivo, otro adverbio o un verbo. Van justo antes de la palabra que modifican: 'very cold', 'almost finished'. Excepción: 'enough' va después del adjetivo o adverbio: 'old enough', 'fast enough'.
types.formation_es: Muchos son palabras fijas (very, quite, too, so, enough). Otros vienen de adjetivo + -ly (extreme → extremely, complete → completely, full → fully). ¡Cuidado con los pares! hard (duro) ≠ hardly (apenas); high (alto) ≠ highly (muy, altamente); near (cerca) ≠ nearly (casi).

items.ex: The soup is very hot, so be careful.
The final exam was extremely difficult.
The movie was quite good, but a bit long.
Her English is fairly good for a beginner.
It's rather cold today, isn't it?
The test was pretty easy, so I finished early.
This coffee is too sweet for me.
Are you old enough to drive a car?
I'm so happy to see you again!
This song is really popular in Colombia right now.
I almost missed the bus this morning.
Dinner is nearly ready, so wash your hands.
I'm sorry, I completely forgot about your birthday.
I totally agree with you about the new rules.
The view from the mountain is absolutely amazing.
Whether you stay or go, the decision is entirely yours.
The hotel is fully booked this weekend.
I could barely hear the teacher from the back.
I could hardly believe my eyes.
There was scarcely any food left after the party.
The price is slightly higher than last year.
I'm a bit tired after the long trip.
Can you speak a little slower, please?
This restaurant is highly recommended by tourists.
The concert last night was incredibly loud.
I'm terribly sorry for the delay.
We were deeply moved by her speech.
The accident was partly my fault.
The results were somewhat disappointing this year.
The players were utterly exhausted after the match.
This phone is much cheaper than mine.
I like this city a lot; the people are friendly.
She speaks remarkably good English for her age.

types.rule_es: Muestran qué tan seguros estamos de algo. Normalmente van antes del verbo principal y después de 'be' o del primer auxiliar: 'It will probably rain', 'She is definitely coming'. 'Maybe' y 'perhaps' suelen ir al inicio de la oración. En negativas van antes de 'won't/don't': 'He probably won't come'.
types.formation_es: La mayoría son adjetivo + -ly (certain → certainly, probable → probably, possible → possibly; -le → -ly). 'Maybe' (may + be) y 'perhaps' son palabras fijas. 'Of course', 'for sure' y 'no doubt' son expresiones.

items.ex: I'll definitely call you tomorrow after work.
It will probably rain this afternoon.
This is possibly the best pizza in town.
She certainly knows how to cook a good sancocho.
Perhaps we should leave earlier tomorrow.
Maybe I'll visit you in Cartagena next month.
He was clearly nervous before the interview.
Surely you don't believe that crazy story!
She is undoubtedly the best player on the team.
He obviously didn't read the instructions.
Prices will very likely rise again next year.
The train is late, presumably because of the weather.
She was evidently upset about the results.
Of course I'll help you with your homework.
No doubt you've already heard the news.
I'll be at your party on Saturday for sure.
He will doubtless become a great doctor one day.
The new phone is supposedly waterproof.
The project could conceivably be finished by June.
We will most likely move to Cali next year.
This is without doubt the hottest day of the year.
The film is undeniably beautiful, but very slow.
Inevitably, the traffic got worse after the holiday.
The seemingly simple task took us three hours.
Shakira is unquestionably one of Colombia's most famous singers.

types.q: What do you think about it?
types.rule_es: Expresan la opinión o actitud del hablante sobre toda la oración. Normalmente van al inicio, seguidos de coma: 'Unfortunately, the museum is closed'. También pueden ir antes del verbo principal.
types.formation_es: Casi todos son adjetivo + -ly (lucky → luckily, honest → honestly, surprising → surprisingly; -ic → -ically: ironic → ironically). ¡Falsos amigos! 'actually' = en realidad (no 'actualmente'); 'eventually' = al final (no 'eventualmente').

items.ex: Unfortunately, the museum is closed on Mondays.
Fortunately, nobody was hurt in the accident.
Luckily, I found my passport just before the flight.
Frankly, I don't think this plan will work.
Honestly, I didn't like the movie very much.
Surprisingly, the cheap hotel was the best one.
Hopefully, the weather will be better tomorrow.
Apparently, the concert has been postponed until May.
Interestingly, most of the students preferred paper books.
Obviously, you need a passport to travel abroad.
Sadly, the old theater closed last year.
Naturally, the children were excited about the trip.
Personally, I prefer the beach to the mountains.
Strangely, nobody answered the phone at the office.
Amazingly, my grandfather's old car still works perfectly.
Ideally, you should sleep eight hours a night.
Admittedly, the hotel was expensive, but the service was excellent.
Thankfully, the rain stopped before the wedding.
Seriously, you need to see a doctor about that cough.
Basically, the job involves answering customer emails.
Actually, I'm from Pereira, not Manizales.
Ironically, the fire station burned down last night.
Understandably, the passengers were angry about the delay.
Oddly, the shop was empty on a Saturday afternoon.
Technically, tomatoes are a fruit, not a vegetable.
The politician allegedly accepted money from a construction company.
Curiously, the dog didn't bark at the stranger.
To be honest, I forgot to do the homework.

types.rule_es: Señalan o limitan la parte de la oración que es importante. Normalmente van antes del verbo principal o justo antes de la palabra que enfocan: 'Only students can enter', 'I eat mainly vegetables'. 'Too', 'as well' y 'either' van al final.
types.formation_es: Algunos son palabras fijas (only, just, even, also). Otros son adjetivo + -ly (main → mainly, simple → simply, particular → particularly). 'Either' (tampoco) se usa solo en oraciones negativas; en afirmativas usa 'too' o 'as well'.

items.ex: Only students can use the library on Sundays.
I just want a glass of water, thanks.
Even my grandmother uses WhatsApp now.
She speaks English, and she also speaks Portuguese.
I like salsa, and my friends like it too.
Can I come to the party as well?
I don't like horror movies either.
I love fruit, especially mango with salt and lime.
The museum is particularly busy on Sundays.
The students in this class are mainly from Bogotá.
The audience was mostly teenagers and their parents.
I simply don't have time to go to the gym.
It was merely a suggestion, not an order.
The decision was based solely on cost.
We met purely by chance at the airport.
The course is primarily for adults who work.
Despite a few problems, the project was largely successful.
That's exactly what I wanted to say.
I specifically asked for a table near the window.
The town is known chiefly for its excellent coffee.
Tourism alone brings millions of dollars to the region.
At least we didn't miss the flight.
This offer is available exclusively to members.
Several cities, notably Bogotá, have built new bike lanes.
I enjoyed the concert, in particular the drums.

types.rule_es: Conectan dos oraciones independientes mostrando su relación (contraste, resultado, adición...). Van al inicio de la segunda oración con coma, o después de punto y coma: '...; however, ...'. No pueden unir dos oraciones solo con una coma.
types.formation_es: Muchos son palabras compuestas (how + ever, there + fore, never + the + less). Otros vienen de adjetivo + -ly (consequent → consequently, similar → similarly). Algunas son expresiones de varias palabras (in addition, as a result).

items.ex: The flight was cheap. However, it had two long stops.
He was sick; therefore, he stayed at home.
The apartment is spacious. Moreover, it has a great view.
It rained all night; consequently, the roads were flooded.
The task was difficult. Nevertheless, we finished on time.
I'll cook dinner. Meanwhile, you can set the table.
Wear a jacket; otherwise, you'll be cold tonight.
The job pays well. Furthermore, it offers flexible hours.
We didn't go to the beach. Instead, we visited a museum.
The company cut costs and thus avoided bankruptcy.
He grew up in London, hence his British accent.
I'm too tired to go out. Besides, it's raining.
The hotel was old. Still, it was clean and comfortable.
My father became a doctor, and I plan to do likewise.
Spanish comes from Latin. Similarly, Italian has Latin roots.

items.es: en consecuencia / de acuerdo con eso
items.ex: Prices went up, so we changed our budget accordingly.
The exam was hard; nonetheless, she passed with a high score.
If you're tired, then you should go to bed.
The plan was risky. Indeed, many experts were against it.
He was arrested and subsequently released without charges.

items.es: a la inversa / por el contrario
items.ex: Some people love the heat; conversely, others prefer the cold.
Incidentally, have you seen my blue jacket anywhere?
It was expensive, but I bought it anyway.
The course is free. In addition, you get a certificate.
He trained every day. As a result, he won the race.
